Bad match for my Kenmore Series 70 dryer - The parts did not match up precisely with my Kenmore Dryer. Sure, the big heating coil and the thermostat were a good match. But the sheet metal screws to affix the thermostat didn't work. The spade on the jumper was not the same size as the connector on my dryer. So, I had to manually modify both. You shouldn't have to do that!

I did manage to successfully install the heater unit and it works. But I spent about 45 minutes making the modifications I needed. And, by the way, I do NOT like modifying electrical equipment. It is not a good practice.

Maybe if you buy one of the other brands, it will fit your Kenmore Series 70.

The filter does its job. Let's see how long it lasts. - So far this water filter seems to be doing its job. It was a snap to install in my Samsung refrigerator. Why am I giving it 3 stars? Two reasons (1) the filter is pricey and (2) let's see how long the filter lasts before the red "needs replacement" LED lights up on the fridge panel. If the filter lasts a long time I will upgrade my rating to 4 or even 5 stars. If the filter doesn't last more than say a few months, then my rating will remain as is or possibly get lowered. I expect a $30 filter to last at least a year.

I brought lowered the ranking from 3 starts to 2 stars because it hasn't been a month since I bought this filter and the red light on my fridge is starting to glow indicating that I might need to replace this filter soon. A $30 filter should last more than a month.

Latest Update: The product just doesn't last. If I consider all the ice cubes and water we used that went through this filter, I don't think it amounts to a 5 gallon jug of water. This product is very, very expensive if you consider the time it lasts. Maybe the product (or the Samsung fridge) is designed to deliberately fail after a short period of time so the customer can keep repurchasing the product. this is called planned obsolescence. Needless to say we bought a generic 2-pack filter this time around.

Love the range, but... - Folks, having two ovens is the bee's knees! Controls are easy to use, too. And my electric bill plunged once we got our old, coil-style electric range removed and this one up and running.

Which brings me to my caveat. It has NOTHING to do with the look pr functionality of this range, which is tops. But I live in a rural area--that's why I have to shop for appliances on Amazon. Which means, once we'd hauled the range inside (and up the stairs--thedelivery guy will bring it to the sidewalk in front of your door) and hooked it up, we then had to deal with a local authorized repair company, and that was nightmarish. It took a MONTH for them to get it working...and kt was not a problem with the unit, only inexperience on the repairman's part. I was repeatedly told that these new-fangled stoves were unreliable and that coil burners were better, Consumer Reports said it was a troublesome brand (though I had used CR as a guide in choosing the product, including reliability), blah blah blah.

I suppose the moral of my story is that you can join the 21st century with a glasstop range, but if your repair people are still using wood-burning stoves you're in for a shock.

Oh! Other things. The stove did not come with a power cord (?!) but the seller called us about that while the range was in transit, gave us a $25 credit, and our local hardware store had one for $20, so yay. And the support personnel at Frigidaire were awesome, even though they were hamstrung by our local company. With their help we finally got 'er done!

It works great, looks identical to the original - This was a good value since all the components are included in the even that the other components besides the heating element need to be replace. Mine only need the heating element, but had this been a more difficult job, I would have gone ahead an replaced the other components. I had to remove 5 screws & the housing slides ride out, and the heating element came out with some light tapping with a rubber mallet. The new element slid in and fit perfectly with only hand pressure and looks to be the same quality as the original. Be sure and take a pic of the wires before disconnecting them, otherwise it will be a bit confusing when you try to reconnect without a clear guide. The entire job took me about an hour because I cleaned out all of the excess lint that had collected throughout the internals of the dryer. I hadn't cleaned it out in several years and it should be done regularly. As far as durability of the new element, I'll update the review if it doesn't last at least a couple of years.

Buying a Bertazzoni appliance set was a BIG mistake - At the urging of the salesman at our local appliance store (locally owned-not a big box) we bought a 36" induction cook top, the 30" wall oven and the matching convection microwave from Bertazzoni. 10K later we are extremely unhappy with them.
After multiple breakdowns of the induction cooktop it was finally deemed a lemon by Bertazzoni (the user interface on this was also a nightmare). We got a Jenn-Air to replace it (so much happier with it)
The wall oven is a very small cavity, does not really accommodate American style pans, the setting of temperature is very imprecise (a rotary dial with no read out on the actual temp) the stupid lights in the oven are on if the oven is on.....what waste of electricity and the very bright lights are annoying. Both wall oven and microwave are NOT user friendly. What should be an easy setting requires a trip to the user manual.
The microwave/convection is a joke. We never ever use the convection oven part (big waste of money). When the cycle has completed you are unable to just simply add more time if needed. You either have to open the door to reset or push off to allow any input of additional time. SO annoying.
For the price being charged you would be better off with Jenn-Air or some other company. We feel totally stuck with these appliances and feel very ripped off by both Bertazzoni and the store we got them from

Consider getting a transparent hose - Is this a dishwasher hose or a clothes-washing machine hose? It seems targeted at both since it has the bracket for a washing machine and the universal end for a dishwasher. Both hose types are essentially the same as long as they fit. This product is more suitable for a washing machine than a dishwasher, but it should work for both.

This is a fine dishwasher hose that you can cut to the right exit diameter. In addition to the exit diameter, make sure the end will fit as there are L-shaped and straight ends. For going into the garbage disposal, having a straight end at that location reduces clogging. Confirm the length you need. If you need to wrap the hose over the top of the dishwasher to get to the drain then 6 ft will not be long enough. This comes with two smaller clamps and one larger clamp, in addition to the extension connector and a hose holder if this is used with a clothes washing machine. For a washing machine, 6ft should be fine.

I have done a lot of dishwasher troubleshooting as a manager of rental properties. Most dishwasher drain hoses I encounter are somewhat transparent. I can see water and debris flowing through them and can see accumulated debris. This is useful when troubleshooting a drainage issue or investigating a possible clog. While not essential, since transparent hoses are so readily available, why not get one of those instead of this opaque one? The transparent ones are the hazy white-colored one that allows light through. I have never had a washing machine drain clog, so for that this opaque color is fine.

This is a generic Chinese hose and the identical product is being sold under different Amazon listings.

Too short, difficult to set up, but otherwise okay. - Pros:
1. Uses a standard Edison plug (i.e. parallel blade with a ground). This can be either a pro or a con. For me it was problematic because the outlet for my washer and dryer was on only a 20 amp circuit. A 30-amp dryer plug would have been more convenient for me. That said, it is nice to know that I can use this dryer if my next apartment doesn't have a dryer outlet.
2. Decent little workhorse--takes some time to get things dry, but it does what it's designed to do.
3. Lightweight--I don't feel like I'll be over-burdening my friends if I ever ask them to help me move.
Cons:
1. It's far too short -- plan on either mounting it to the wall, building a pedestal, or developing back problems. If I were to recommend a redesign for the next model it would be to put the controls near the top.
2. The vent on the back is a non-standard size (about 3 3/8 inches). This made putting a dryer tube on the back a pain. I followed the advice of another reviewer and removed some of the wire from a 4" wide flexible aluminum duct and was able to clamp it on with some careful finagling.
3. Drum wouldn't spin on first running the machine. I had to open it up and wrap the belt around the drum to get it to spin (I don't really knock stars off for this, since it happens from time to time; but I mention it for anyone who does buy it--if it doesn't spin at first, unplug it, take of the back panel and have a look before returning it -- saved me a shipping headache).

Overall:
If your choice is no dryer or this dryer, buy this dryer. I really like having a dryer, but I don't particularly like having this dryer. Between it's height and the difficulty attaching the hose to the vent, I don't think I'd buy it again. That said, it is a decent bargain, and it does the job I need it to do. I can't hate it too much.
